model: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: organic same-store revenue growth (occupancy + rate), year 1 of the base path -- not a historical CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity (20.5-26.9%) and revenue (18.7-22.7%) CAGRs are inflated by stock-funded acquisitions: diluted shares rose from 417M (FY2020) to 697M (FY2025) and 755M (Q3-26). They are not per-share growth and are unusable as a growth proxy. GAAP EPS CAGRs are noise (disposal gains, impairments, the FY2025 ECAP charge).
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGR is computed on FFO PER SHARE, the per-share flow this model capitalises: FY2022 USD 3.18 -> FY2025 ~USD 4.78 excluding the USD 1.41bn ECAP charge (reported USD 2.68) = 14.5% 3-year. No 5-year figure: the FFO series in the Metrics CSV starts at FY2021 (USD 2.86). All CAGRs end at FY2025, the last full fiscal year.

scenario_narratives.base: Welltower has turned itself into a seniors-housing operating business: resident fees are 84% of revenue, outpatient medical is being sold, and same-store NOI is growing 17% (seniors housing 20%+) as occupancy recovers from 78% in 2022 to 88.3%. The base case lets that recovery finish -- occupancy to ~92% by year 4, rate growth of 4-5%, operating leverage taking the FFO margin from 32% to 40% -- and then settles to inflation-plus growth. It is organic only on a flat share count: no credit for future acquisitions, and no charge for the equity that would fund them. FFO per share roughly doubles, from USD 6.18 to about USD 13.7 after SBC, over ten years.
scenario_narratives.bull: The 80-plus population grows faster than at any time on record through the mid-2030s while construction starts sit at multi-decade lows, so occupancy pushes through 94% and pricing power persists. The data-science operating platform keeps widening margins, and the equity currency -- issued far above net asset value -- keeps buying 6-7% yields accretively, adding 2-3 points of per-share growth for five years. This needs demand, supply discipline and the premium multiple all to hold at once.
scenario_narratives.bear: Seniors housing is a short-lease, labour-intensive operating business and has had supply cycles before (2016-2019). Today's rents and margins invite construction; occupancy stalls around 89-90%, care-staff wages and insurance take the rate increases, and margins plateau at 34.5%. Capital needs stay elevated on a large, ageing estate. Growth falls to 2.5-3% by year 5. Nothing here is distress -- leverage is low -- it is simply a normal REIT growth rate applied to a stock priced for something else.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Welltower is valued as a stream of post-interest AFFO per share capitalised at the cost of equity, with debt left where it is. The business quality is not in doubt: low leverage, 17% same-store NOI growth, a long demographic runway. The issue is price. At the current quote the stock trades at roughly 40x run-rate normalised FFO and above 50x owner AFFO, a 1.4% dividend yield. Even a base case that doubles FFO per share organically in ten years, discounted at 9.25%, supports about half the price; the bull case does not reach it either. The gap is the market capitalising external growth funded by richly valued equity -- a loop that works while the multiple holds and is not something a holder of the existing shares can count on at a 9% required return.
key_risks_to_valuation: FY0 FFO is the analyst's normalisation of Q3-2026 (transaction costs added back, 25M/quarter retained); the company's own normalized FFO from the 8-K supplemental was not available and may differ by a few percent.
AFFO deductions are a judgment: half of renovation/redevelopment capex is charged as maintenance. Charging none of it raises value ~10%; charging all of it lowers it ~10%.

Organic-only growth on a flat share count excludes accretion from issuing equity above NAV, the main reason the market price exceeds this model. If the premium multiple persists for many years the base case is too low; if it closes, external growth stops being accretive.
Seniors-housing supply response and care-labour inflation are the operating swing factors; occupancy at 88.3% leaves perhaps 4-6 points of recovery before pricing alone must carry growth.
The 10-Year ECAP pre-paid a decade of executive equity pay (USD 1.41bn in Q4-2025); reported SBC and FFO understate steady-state compensation until it is renewed.
Cost of equity sensitivity: a long-duration flow, so each 1pp of discount rate moves value by roughly 15-20%.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 181.47-255.20
data_sources.financials: WELL_Metrics.csv / WELL.duckdb (core_metrics, kpis: FFO, FFOPerShare, SameStoreNOI, occupancy); Q3-2026 10-Q (balance sheet, cash flow, EPS note, stock incentive note, FFO reconciliation, capex table, leverage table); FY2025 10-K
data_sources.qualitative: FY2025 10-K and Q3-2026 10-Q MD&A read directly; WELL_Analysis.json was not yet available

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 30-Sep-2026: 731.995M common outstanding (10-Q leverage table) + 30.574M dilutive potential shares from the Q3-26 EPS note (13.137M OP/DownREIT units incl. the 10-Year ECAP LTIP units, 10.162M unvested restricted shares/units, 6.374M exchangeable-note shares, 0.876M options, 0.025M ESPP). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows and the growth paths are organic only, so no ATM issuance is modelled.
inputs.debt_memo: NOT deducted: the capitalised flow is post-interest FFO/AFFO, so subtracting debt would count it twice. Balance sheet at 30-Sep-2026 (USD M): unsecured credit facility + CP 1,041.1; senior unsecured notes 14,687.0; secured debt 3,467.1 = 19,195.2 (company long-term debt obligations incl. finance leases 18,631.0 + 1,041.1); cash 2,274.9 + restricted 141.1; company-defined net debt 17,256.1 = 26% of book capitalisation, 9% of enterprise value. Operating lease liabilities 1,968.1 (ground leases; rent is inside property opex).
inputs.sbc_source: Q3-2026 10-Q stock incentive plan note: Q3 total 22.268M (incl. 10.656M 10-Year ECAP incremental cost), annualised. 9M-2026 cash-flow add-back 57.618M. Equity-award withholding taxes are immaterial (treasury stock movement ~12M YTD) and not added. FFO as reported is already after this expense; it is added back to form the engine's pre-SBC margin and then charged once via sbc_pct_path.
inputs.fy0_basis: FY0 is the Q3-2026 ANNUALISED RUN-RATE, not the calendar-year total: revenue 3,715.8 x 4; normalised FFO 1,177 x 4 = 4,709 (USD 6.18 per fully diluted share). A run-rate base is required because 9M-2026 saw USD 9.7bn of acquisitions funded by USD 7.5bn of new equity: a calendar-year flow would pair nine months of a smaller portfolio with the period-end share count.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-13T21:02:42Z regular close (Friday; valuation run on a weekend)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of EQUITY, not WACC, because the flow is post-interest. USD build: 10-year UST 5.15% (Yahoo ^TNX, 2026-11-13) + beta 0.82 x 5.0% ERP = 9.25%. Beta sits below SPG (0.9) and near O/MAA because leverage is very low (net debt 9% of EV, 26% of book cap) but above PSA because 84% of revenue is RIDEA seniors-housing operating income with direct labour-cost and occupancy exposure. Same rate in all three scenarios: risk is charged once, through the scenario weights.
inputs.lease_treatment: Ground/operating lease rent is inside property operating expenses and therefore already inside FFO; lease liabilities (1,968M) are not deducted. One treatment only.
inputs.nci_treatment: FFO is the company's NAREIT figure attributable to common stockholders after its noncontrolling-interest and unconsolidated-entity adjustments; OP/DownREIT units are in the diluted share count with their income added back. NCI charged once, in the flow.
inputs.ffo_normalisation: Q3-2026 NAREIT FFO 1,070.8M (USD 1.42/sh). Normalised to 1,177M: + 99.7M of the 124.7M 'other expenses' (non-capitalisable acquisition transaction costs and operator-transition/HC-One restructuring costs; 25M per quarter is RETAINED as a recurring cost of running a RIDEA platform) + 6.8M loss on debt extinguishment. The H1-2026 income-tax benefit (~50M) is outside Q3 and so outside the base. The 8-K 'normalized FFO' is not in the extracted filings; this is the analyst's reconstruction from the 10-Q and should be replaced with the company's figure on refresh.
inputs.fy2025_distortion: FY2025 NAREIT FFO (1,818M, USD 2.68/sh) is NOT a usable base: Q4-2025 FFO of -597M carries the ~USD 1.41bn up-front expense of the 10-Year Executive Continuity and Alignment Program (LTIP units fully vested for accounting at grant; FY2025 SBC 1,556.7M vs 75.8M in FY2024). Ex-ECAP FY2025 FFO is ~3,228M (~USD 4.78/sh). The ECAP is charged once here: its LTIP units are in the diluted count (OP units 13.1M vs 2.6M a year earlier), and only the ongoing incremental cost (10.7M/quarter) is in the forward SBC line. Because the grant pre-pays ten years of executive equity pay, sbc_pct_path rises back to the pre-ECAP 0.95% of revenue by the terminal year to fund its renewal.
inputs.affo_bridge: Engine mapping: 'EBITDA margin' = (normalised FFO + SBC) / revenue = (4,709 + 89) / 14,863 = 32.3%. D&A and cash tax are zero (FFO is post-depreciation add-back and the REIT pays ~no entity tax; TRS tax is inside FFO). 'Capex' = the FFO-to-AFFO deductions, 8.1% of revenue at FY0 (1,204M): recurring capex, tenant improvements and lease commissions 441M (331.0M 9M-26, annualised) 3.0%; non-cash rent in excess of cash received 350M (262.6M 9M-26) 2.4%; and HALF of 'renovations, redevelopments and other capital improvements' 404M (606.1M 9M-26) 2.7% -- the half treated as the price of keeping a 20-year-old seniors-housing estate competitive, the other half and all new development (360.4M 9M-26) treated as growth capex whose return is not in the organic growth path. FY0 owner AFFO = 4,709 - 1,204 = 3,505M = USD 4.60/sh; dividend USD 3.40/sh annualised (74% payout).
inputs.notes: MODEL: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the Drivers engine with net debt held at zero (same pattern as O, PSA, SPG, MAA). Routed by dcf-methods SKILL.md: a REIT's cash flow is post-interest, so an owner-FCF/WACC/net-debt build would deduct the debt twice, and GAAP net income is dominated by disposal gains (USD 634M in 9M-2026) and depreciation. First valuation of this ticker; no prior model. Price is a regular-session close, not an after-hours print. Buybacks: none (WELL is a serial net ISSUER -- USD 7.5bn of common stock in 9M-2026 via the ATM); the flat count is a modelling convention matched to organic-only growth paths, and the accretion from issuing equity above NAV appears only in the bull case's growth. Qualitative context taken directly from the FY2025 10-K and Q3-2026 10-Q: WELL_Analysis.json had not been written when this model was built. Seniors-housing occupancy 88.3% (Q3-26) vs 78.0% (Q3-22); same-store NOI growth 16.8% total, 20.5% seniors housing, 2.3% outpatient medical (being sold: USD 7.2bn, 319-property disposal announced Aug-2025, closing in tranches).

bear.narrative: Occupancy stalls near 89-90% as new supply responds to today's rents, wage inflation in care staff absorbs the rate increases, and an ageing estate needs more capital to hold its position.

base.narrative: Organic only. Seniors-housing occupancy climbs from 88.3% to ~92% by year 4 and holds; RevPOR grows 4-5%; operating leverage lifts the FFO margin from 32.3% to 40%. FFO per share compounds ~15% in year 1 fading to ~4% by year 10.

bull.narrative: Demographic wave plus a decade of under-building: occupancy reaches ~94-95%, RevPOR outruns labour cost for longer, and equity issued well above NAV keeps funding acquisitions accretively (2-3pp of per-share growth in years 1-5).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): the balance sheet carries no refinancing risk, but the earnings are operating income on monthly leases with a history of supply cycles, so a plateau is more likely than for a net-lease REIT. Base 50%: it already assumes the occupancy recovery completes and margins expand eight points. Bull 30% (below the 35% default): it needs demographics, muted supply and a continuing premium equity currency to hold together.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
